# Long-form visual explainers

The job is sustained understanding. Use readable prose and integrated visual reasoning: calm enough to follow the argument, interactive where manipulating a relationship or watching a change adds understanding. The reader should not have to choose between reading and enjoying the presentation.

This is different from a quick internal ELI5 brief. Depth is appropriate here; unnecessary prose and distracting spectacle are not.

## Approved calibration pair

| Reference | What to study and borrow |
|---|---|
| [Load Balancing — Sam Rose](https://samwho.dev/load-balancing/) | A systems article whose request/server simulations progress from one server to overload and multiple servers. Matching shapes and colors connect prose to the simulation; local pause controls let the reader set the pace. |
| [A Friendly Introduction to Spring Physics — Josh W. Comeau](https://www.joshwcomeau.com/animation/a-friendly-introduction-to-spring-physics/) | A physics tutorial with a two-ball animation comparison and a draggable spring weight. Changing mass affects both the illustrated weight and numerical configuration. Borrow the close connection between explanation, manipulation and feedback. |

## Established references

| Reference | What to study and borrow |
|---|---|
| [Multimodal Neurons — Distill](https://distill.pub/2021/multimodal-neurons/) | Research article with aligned biological/model-neuron image comparisons and categorized galleries that expand in place. Study how metadata, restrained typography and visual evidence support the argument together. |
| [A Visual Exploration of Gaussian Processes — Distill](https://distill.pub/2019/visual-exploration-gaussian-processes/) | Mathematical explainer pairing prediction lines with uncertainty bands, then aligned kernel equations and heatmaps. Local sliders change the associated matrix; small comparisons build intuition without turning the page into a show. |
| [How to Use t-SNE Effectively — Distill](https://distill.pub/2016/misread-tsne/) | Parameter-comparison article: an original dataset sits beside multiple result plots with explicit perplexity/step labels. Result tiles open live experiments. Borrow comparisons that make parameter sensitivity inspectable. |
| [A Visual Introduction to Machine Learning — R2D3](http://www.r2d3.us/visual-intro-to-machine-learning-part-1/) | Machine-learning explainer coordinating short passages with an evolving visualization; guide the reader rather than dropping them into a sandbox. |
| [Understanding UMAP — Google PAIR](https://pair-code.github.io/understanding-umap/) | Technical article with separate data and algorithm controls, a Play-driven transformation and a visible step counter. Explanations lead into manipulable figures, giving exploration a question rather than merely a control panel. |

## Visual-intensity boundary

[Dithering — Part 1](https://visualrambling.space/dithering-part-1/) is a stepped visual introduction: arrow keys or screen-side taps advance captions over a transforming black-and-white pixel field on yellow. Its craft and motion are admired, but its intensity competed with reading in calibration. Borrow an explanatory transition or pixel technique, not the overall intensity; leave the idea in charge of attention.
